sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- UKMTO weekly report, via Al Jazeera Nov 7] At least 11 ships were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the week ending November 6, and three of them sank. UKMTO counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits in the strait, approximately 65 percent below pre-conflict levels. UKMTO separately recorded 155 vessel security incidents linked to the US-Iran conflict within its monitoring area so far this year (Bastille Post relay, Nov 7). [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Iranian Navy, via IRNA/Press TV, Nov 7] An oil tanker caught fire early Saturday morning after hitting a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz while sailing through a prohibited and unsafe zone; the vessel had switched off its navigation systems and ignored repeated warnings; it was left immobile; no casualty information reported. The navy warned this would be the fate of all vessels violating restrictions. [CONTEXT -- already recorded] IRGC's five-tankers-plus-tug mine claims recorded at 1000-04 (HOLD, no independent confirmation); IMO: 25 seafarers killed, 130 attacks since Feb 28 (1000-01, PASS); Velos Sapphire fatality recorded (1000-01); UKMTO Warning 197-26 Khasab waterline explosion recorded (1000-02). [PORTWATCH -- STALE] Newest IMF PortWatch snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, stale=true, latest observation 2026-10-18 (Hormuz 4 transits, 7-day avg 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day). The UKMTO weekly report is the fresh counted source for this hour; do NOT cite PortWatch as current.
sections.what_verified: UKMTO weekly report carried by Al Jazeera (T2); UKMTO is itself the T1 primary source for maritime incidents; DeepDraft SITREP and Bastille Post relay the same UKMTO data (untiered, attribution only).
sections.what_disputed: Washington says the mines have been cleared (Al Jazeera article, Nov 7). Reuters: no confirmation from maritime officials of the IRGC mine claims (recorded 1000-04). The Saturday tanker is unnamed, no flag, no casualty details; the mine-hit attribution is the Iranian navy's alone. A news-brief.com aggregator piece circulating today adds uncorroborated claims (Brent $88.70, UNSC emergency session, Ansar Allah ceasefire suspension) -- see triage 1700-07(c); do not cite.
sections.why_matters: Counted, not claimed: UKMTO's own weekly report puts 11 ships attacked and 3 sunk in one week, transits down 65% -- while Iran says mines did it and Washington says the mines are cleared. Who is telling the truth about the strait?
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (Al Jazeera article published 2026-11-07T12:22:18Z = 16:22 ; zero '11 ships'/'3 sank'/'170 outbound' mentions in any prior Nov 6/7 scan -- grep confirms) -- UKMTO weekly report: 11 ships attacked in/around Hormuz in week ending Nov 6, 3 sank; transits ~65% below pre-conflict; PLUS Iranian navy says a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine east of Hormuz on Saturday morning

totw_analysis: Our read: Counted, not claimed: UKMTO's own weekly report puts 11 ships attacked and 3 sunk in one week, transits down 65% -- while Iran says mines did it and Washington says the mines are cleared. Who is telling the truth about the strait? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Mines or missiles -- who is really sinking ships in Hormuz, and can anyone still sail it?
